findings.description: The human surface has no automated regression. All three tests in crates/app/tests/adapter_catalog.rs pass --json, and crates/cli has no unit tests, so the not-detected-installations label, the hint and capability lines and the human-failure stderr routing are protected by nothing in the four declared checks; they rest on one-time captures in catalog-human-smoke.json, catalog-human-error-smoke.json and a real-PTY observation. The behavior is correct today - I read the code and the captures agree - so this is a durability gap rather than a defect. It matters because the missing protection sits on the one line whose whole job is to stop a human reading a plausible path as a discovery; docs/cli.md's disclaimer that human layouts are not machine-stable covers layout, not that product property. Cheap encoding: a fourth case in the file that already exists, using the existing catalog() helper, asserting the human stdout contains the label and that --human with a bad argument yields empty stdout, exit 2 and a stderr message free of the hostile token. Accepted and non-blocking; worth doing before the next adapter lands.
